---
title: Scheduling, clock, and sound
---

## The clock

A Sign keeps its own time, date, and day of the week. `{time}` and `{date}` show
them, and Run Times are measured on them. Set all three at once:

```python
from datetime import datetime

sign.set_clock(datetime.now())
```

Seconds are dropped. The Sign stores a two-digit year, read as 1997-2096, so a
date outside those years raises `ValueError`.

Choose 12-hour or 24-hour time:

```python
from alpha_led_sign import TimeFormat

sign.set_time_format(TimeFormat.TWENTY_FOUR_HOUR)
```

## Which TEXT Files run, and when

The Run Sequence is the list of TEXT Files the Sign shows in turn:

```python
sign.run_sequence("ABC")
```

Each File then runs during its Run Time, a daily start and stop time in
10-minute steps. Set it in the Memory Configuration (`TextFile(..., run_time=...)`)
or later, for any Files you name:

```python
from datetime import time

from alpha_led_sign import RunTime

sign.set_run_times({
    "A": RunTime.between(time(8, 0), time(17, 0)),
    "B": RunTime.ALWAYS,
    "C": RunTime.NEVER,
})
```

A time that is not on a 10-minute step raises `ValueError`. `RunTime.ALWAYS`,
`RunTime.NEVER`, and `RunTime.ALL_DAY` are the manual's special Run Times; a new
`TextFile` defaults to `ALWAYS`.

Run Days limit a File to some days of the week:

```python
from alpha_led_sign import RunDay, RunDays, Weekday

sign.set_run_days({
    "A": RunDays(RunDay.WEEKDAYS),
    "B": RunDays(RunDay.MONDAY, Weekday.THURSDAY),   # Monday to Thursday
})
```

`RunDay` has single days, `DAILY`, `WEEKDAYS`, `WEEKENDS`, `ALWAYS`, and `NEVER`.
The stop day only matters when the start is a single day.

Writing Run Times or Run Days ends a Priority TEXT File.

### Run order

`run_sequence` takes an `order`:

- `RunOrder.BY_RUN_TIME` (the default): each File runs during its Run Time.
- `RunOrder.IN_ORDER`: every File runs in turn, ignoring Run Times.
- `RunOrder.DELETE_WHEN_DONE`: each File runs during its Run Time, and is deleted
  when its stop time passes.

Pass `locked=True` to stop the Run Sequence being changed from the IR keyboard.

## Sound

The speaker is off when a Sign powers up. Turn it on first:

```python
from alpha_led_sign import Tone

sign.set_speaker(True)
sign.beep()                       # three short beeps
sign.beep(Tone.CONTINUOUS)        # about 2 seconds
sign.tone(frequency=100, duration=5, repeats=2)
```

`tone` plays for `duration` tenths of a second (1-15), then plays again `repeats`
more times (0-15). A 4120C plays every `frequency` at the same pitch.

The Sign can't take data while it plays a tone. `beep` waits 3 s before it returns,
and `tone` waits until the last repeat has finished.
